    label_replace(

panels.title: ml-api HTTP response status
panels.description: Requests handled by ml-api per interval, by endpoint and HTTP status code. Health, readiness and metrics endpoints are excluded. Any 5xx series is a server-side failure.

targets.expr: sum by (pod) (backend_api_db_connections_active{namespace="backend-api", job="backend-api", container="backend-api"})

panels.title: backend-api database connections in use
panels.description: Database connections each backend-api pod currently has in use (backend_api_db_connections_active). The dashed line at 10 is the size of the per-pod connection pool; a pod sitting at the line has no free connections and further requests fail with 503 and are counted as pool_exhausted.
Database queries issued by backend-api per interval, by outcome (backend_api_db_queries_total). Anything other than "success" is a failed query.
panels.title: backend-api database queries by status

targets.expr: sum by (pod) (ml_api_memory_bytes{namespace="ml-api", job="ml-api", container="ml-api"})
sum by (pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace="ml-api", container="ml-api", image!=""})
max(kube_pod_container_resource_limits{namespace="ml-api", container="ml-api", resource="memory"})

panels.title: ml-api application memory
panels.description: Memory the ml-api application reports for itself (ml_api_memory_bytes) per pod, next to the memory the container actually uses and the container memory limit. A steadily rising line that approaches the limit ends in an OOM kill.

targets.expr: sum(rate(ml_api_predictions_total{namespace="ml-api", job="ml-api", container="ml-api"}[$__rate_interval]))
sum(rate(ml_api_requests_total{namespace="ml-api", job="ml-api", container="ml-api", exported_endpoint="/predict"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: ml-api predictions vs requests
panels.description: Predictions completed per second (ml_api_predictions_total) next to incoming /predict requests per second. The two lines normally lie on top of each other; predictions falling below requests means requests are failing or hanging before a prediction is produced.

targets.expr: sum by (datname, state) (pg_stat_activity_count{datname="voize"})

panels.title: voize database connections
panels.description: Connections to the voize database as postgres sees them (pg_stat_activity), by state. Idle connections are open but not running a query, typically held by connection pools; active ones are running a query.

All client connections to the postgres server as a share of max_connections. Close to 100% new connections are refused (postgres keeps a few slots, superuser_reserved_connections, for superusers only).

targets.expr:
sum(pg_stat_activity_count{namespace="postgres"})
/
max(pg_settings_max_connections{namespace="postgres"})

panels.title: postgres connection limit usage

panels.description: Age of the oldest open transaction in the voize database, for running queries (active) and for sessions holding a transaction open without doing anything (idle in transaction). A steadily climbing line means a query is hanging or blocked.
panels.title: voize longest running transaction

panels.description: Locks currently held or awaited in the voize database, by lock mode. A few accesssharelock entries are normal; accessexclusivelock blocks every other query on the table.

targets.expr: sum by (mode) (pg_locks_count{namespace="postgres", datname="voize"}) > 0

panels.title: voize database locks by mode

targets.expr:
max by (namespace, pod) (
    (kube_pod_container_status_ready{namespace=~"backend-api|ml-api|postgres"} == bool 0) == 1
      unless on (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_phase{namespace=~"backend-api|ml-api|postgres", phase="Succeeded"} == 1)
      unless on (namespace, pod) kube_pod_deletion_timestamp{namespace=~"backend-api|ml-api|postgres"}
      unless on (namespace, pod) (time() - kube_pod_start_time{namespace=~"backend-api|ml-api|postgres"} < 60)
  or
    (increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace=~"backend-api|ml-api|postgres"}[$__rate_interval]) > bool 0) == 1
)

panels.title: unhealthy pods
panels.description: Pods in the backend-api, ml-api and postgres namespaces with a container that is not ready or that restarted during the interval, one row per pod. Pods that completed, are being deleted or started less than 60 seconds ago are left out. A green row means all pods were healthy at that time.

targets.expr:
count by (namespace) (time() - kube_pod_created{namespace=~"backend-api|ml-api|postgres"} < 300)
or
count by (namespace) (kube_pod_created{namespace=~"backend-api|ml-api|postgres"}) * 0

panels.title: pods created in the last 5 min
panels.description: Number of pods created within the previous 5 minutes, per namespace. Zero in steady state; a bump marks a restart, rollout or reschedule. Limited to the backend-api, ml-api and postgres namespaces.

Pods that have been in the Pending phase for more than 60 seconds: not yet scheduled to a node (for example requesting more CPU or memory than is available), or scheduled but unable to start their containers (for example an image that cannot be pulled). A green row means no pod was pending at that time. Limited to the backend-api, ml-api and postgres namespaces.

targets.expr:
max by (namespace, pod) (
  (kube_pod_status_phase{namespace=~"backend-api|ml-api|postgres", phase="Pending"} == 1)
  and on (namespace, pod) (time() - kube_pod_created{namespace=~"backend-api|ml-api|postgres"} > 60)
)

panels.title: pending pods

panels.description: Why a pod is failing, one row per pod and reason: containers that cannot start (CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, ...), containers that were killed and restarted (OOMKilled, Error) and pods that cannot be scheduled (Unschedulable). Pods that are running but fail their readiness probe have no reason here; they only appear in "unhealthy pods". Limited to the backend-api, ml-api and postgres namespaces.

targets.expr:
max by (namespace, pod, reason) (
  kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{namespace=~"backend-api|ml-api|postgres", reason!~"ContainerCreating|PodInitializing"} == 1
)
or
max by (namespace, pod, reason) (
  (kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{namespace=~"backend-api|ml-api|postgres"} == 1)
  and on (namespace, pod, container)
  (increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace=~"backend-api|ml-api|postgres"}[$__rate_interval]) > 0)
)
or
label_replace(
  max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_unschedulable{namespace=~"backend-api|ml-api|postgres"} == 1),
  "reason", "Unschedulable", "", ""
)

vector(0) unless on() (
  max by (namespace, pod, reason) (
    kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{namespace=~"backend-api|ml-api|postgres", reason!~"ContainerCreating|PodInitializing"} == 1
  )
  or
  max by (namespace, pod, reason) (
    (kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{namespace=~"backend-api|ml-api|postgres"} == 1)
    and on (namespace, pod, container)
    (increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{namespace=~"backend-api|ml-api|postgres"}[$__rate_interval]) > 0)
  )
  or
  label_replace(
    max by (namespace, pod) (kube_pod_status_unschedulable{namespace=~"backend-api|ml-api|postgres"} == 1),
    "reason", "Unschedulable", "", ""
  )
)

panels.title: pod failure reasons
CPU and memory by workload
panels.description: Current CPU and memory use per workload, with CPU as a share of the CPU request and memory as a share of the memory limit (taken from the container closest to its limit). Limited to the backend-api, ml-api and postgres namespaces.

panels.title: memory usage per pod
panels.description: Memory in use (working set) per pod, for the ten pods using the most. Working set is what counts against the memory limit. Limited to the backend-api, ml-api and postgres namespaces.

panels.title: CPU usage per pod
panels.description: CPU cores in use per pod, for the ten pods using the most. 0.5 means half a core. Limited to the backend-api, ml-api and postgres namespaces.

Share of CPU scheduling periods in which the pod was throttled by its CPU limit. 0% means the limit is never hit; sustained values above roughly 25% usually show up as higher request latency. Limited to the backend-api, ml-api and postgres namespaces.
panels.title: CPU throttling per pod
